profile_text.body:
Microsoft is a Redmond, Washington-based public company founded in 1975 that reported revenue of $331.839 billion for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2026. The company describes Power Automate as a platform for automating workflows and business processes across apps, systems, and websites using AI, digital, and robotic process automation. According to its site, the platform can reduce manual data validation work—one customer example states that a process previously requiring over 100 people can now be managed by a few people with generative AI and Power Automate.

Microsoft's AI product portfolio spans multiple categories. In automation and agents, it offers Microsoft Power Automate AI for enterprise workflow automation with Copilot integration and data loss prevention integration. The company provides Azure OpenAI Service for access to OpenAI models in Azure regions with enterprise content filtering and data residency controls, and Azure Machine Learning as an MLOps platform with AutoML and responsible AI toolkit integration. For chat and general LLMs, Microsoft Copilot is embedded across Microsoft 365. Developer-focused offerings include AutoGen for multi-agent conversation frameworks, Semantic Kernel as a model-agnostic orchestration SDK for .NET, Python, and Java, and Microsoft Agent Framework as a unified successor to both Semantic Kernel and AutoGen. Microsoft also offers Teams AI for meeting recaps and intelligent summaries, SharePoint AI for enterprise content, Microsoft Designer for image generation, and Clipchamp AI for video editing.

Microsoft faces two copyright-related lawsuits in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York: The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. and OpenAI and Authors Guild v. OpenAI, Inc. The company has 96 instances of law exposure identified in Washington state.
